__inputs.name: DS_PROMETHEUS
__inputs.label: Prometheus
__inputs.description: The Prometheus that scrapes the server's /metrics

title: Vault Syncryption
description: The Vault Syncryption server's Prometheus metrics (/metrics).

panels.title: Scrape
panels.description: Whether Prometheus reached /metrics on its last scrape.

panels.title: Version
panels.description: The server version and protocol version (syncryption_build_info).

panels.title: Maintenance
panels.description: Maintenance mode pauses the sync API (503).

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Since the server process started (Linux only).

panels.title: Open long-polls
panels.description: Open /wait requests: roughly the devices online.

panels.title: Active locks
panels.description: Soft locks that haven't expired.

panels.title: Active keys
panels.description: Encryption keys (one per device per vault) that are active.

panels.title: Pending keys
panels.description: Keys waiting for a device of their vault to approve them.

panels.title: Stored
panels.description: Total size of the encrypted blobs.

panels.title: Files
panels.description: Files, deleted ones included until retention drops them.

panels.title: Responses by status
panels.description: 401 and 409 are part of normal sync (expired sessions, conflicts). 503 is maintenance.

panels.title: Latency p50 / p95 / p99 (without long-polls)
panels.description: /wait long-polls are left out: they stay open until something changes or they time out.

panels.title: Cleanup deletions per hour
panels.description: Retention and blob garbage collection run hourly.

panels.title: Cleanup failures
panels.description: Failed hourly runs; the container log has the error.

panels.title: Wrong secrets and tokens per hour
panels.description: Both are rate-limited per address; a steady rise means someone is guessing.

targets.expr: sum by (route, status) (rate(syncryption_http_requests_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance", route=~"/api/v1/auth/.*", status=~"4.."}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: S3 calls by operation
panels.description: Calls the server makes to the S3 bucket for blobs. Empty when blobs are stored in ./data.

panels.title: S3 failures by result
panels.description: Failed S3 calls after botocore's retries: throttled (SlowDown, 503, 429), client_error (other 4xx, e.g. AccessDenied), server_error (5xx), connection (no answer). not_found is left out: a lookup of a missing blob is normal.

panels.title: S3 latency p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description: Duration of the S3 calls for blobs, botocore's retries and reading the body included.

panels.title: S3 throughput
panels.description: Blob bytes uploaded to and downloaded from the bucket.

panels.title: S3 retries by operation
panels.description: Retries botocore made inside S3 calls. Steady retries usually mean the provider is throttling or flaky.

panels.title: Litestream
panels.description: 1 while the server can read Litestream's metrics. Empty without S3: Litestream replicates meta.db only while blobs are stored in S3.

panels.title: Syncs and sync errors
panels.description: Litestream copies new WAL pages into its shadow WAL about once a second; errors usually mean the bucket is unreachable.

panels.title: Time spent syncing
panels.description: Share of time Litestream spends syncing (seconds per second).

panels.title: Uploads to S3
panels.description: Litestream's uploads to the bucket, by operation.

panels.title: Replication throughput
panels.description: WAL bytes Litestream wrote for replication, and bytes it sent to the bucket.

panels.title: Container CPU
panels.description: The whole container: server, Caddy and Litestream. 1 = one core. From the container's cgroup (Linux, cgroup v2).

panels.title: Container memory
panels.description: The whole container: server, Caddy and Litestream. Working set is what docker stats shows and what counts towards the limit; the limit line appears only if the container has one.

panels.title: Server process open files
panels.description: Open file descriptors of the Python server process and its limit. Linux only.

panels.title: Server process CPU
panels.description: Only the Python server process, not Caddy or Litestream. 1 = one core. Linux only.

panels.title: Server process memory
panels.description: Resident memory of the Python server process only, not Caddy or Litestream. Linux only.
